observations.statement: On p1 the first input came 4.2 s after the question appeared; right-hand motion in the 4-12 Hz band was 1.5x the calibration level.
On p2 there were 2 pauses of 3 s or more between inputs and 2 answer changes before the correct submission.
A likely startle when the monster appeared during p3: head rotation peaked far above the level just before it, then a stretch of freezing and a held breath before breathing came back fast.
Head scanning on p4 was 4.6x the calibration level and 4-12 Hz hand motion was 2.6x (right hand).
The session ended during p5 when the game's monster caught the player.

data_quality.statement: Calibration produced a usable baseline and tracking coverage was high on every question.

limitations: Possible states are inferred from motion and breathing by fixed rules. They are probabilities about moments, not diagnoses, and every value is relative to this person's own calm calibration. Fatigue, caffeine, cold, posture or an unfamiliar headset produce the same signals.
Hand motion in the 4-12 Hz band has common medical and physical causes and must not be read as a sign of anything about the person.
This summary does not make, and must not be used as, a hiring decision. The employer decides.
